answer: CloudMind helps you generate secure cloud configurations based on your infrastructure needs.
IAM controls who can do what in your cloud environment. If your IAM policy uses 'Action: *', it exposes a major security risk.
Setting a session timeout ensures that inactive users are logged out automatically to prevent hijacking.
The AI risk score indicates how vulnerable your project is. 1.0 = High Threat, 0.0 = Safe.
Public access exposes your S3 buckets or services to the entire internet. Always disable public access unless strictly necessary.
Repeated failed password attempts suggest a brute-force attack. It's critical to monitor and restrict SSH access.
Duplicate IPs found in log files may indicate a brute-force attack from a single source IP.
CloudTrail captures all cloud API activity. Misconfigured trails can expose sensitive operations.
Every threat has a fix listed in your report. Apply those fixes starting with High severity issues first.
